object_description: single-level school volume with offset classroom wings
design_condition: The building is placed east on the plot, leaving a mineral square to the west and a generous planted playground between the school and the traffic-related areas, although a future extension removes this recreation space.

positive.statement: The undulating distribution space has great spatial richness, reinforced by the slightly offset classroom pairs and glazed ends.

position.rationale: Central offset circulation zone is visible in the top footprint and repeated elevation bands.

positive.statement: The openness and porosity of the project generously bring in views of the surrounding countryside and connect the building with exterior spaces.

position.rationale: Porous elongated volume and exterior connections are evident across the footprint and elevations.

positive.statement: The modest image of added elements and the ecological approach meet the requirements of the brief.

position.rationale: Overall modest expression is assigned to the sampled low-rise envelope; ecological and cost claims are non-geometric.

negative.statement: The future extension regrettably removes the generous recreation space, although additional recreational spaces would be required.

position.rationale: West-side open ground is the plausible location of the removed playground and future extension.

negative.statement: The two separate entrances and absence of a common playground create operating problems for supervising children.

position.rationale: Ground-level end zones approximate entrances and the absent shared playground.

negative.statement: Solar protection for the south-facing classrooms remains unresolved.

position.rationale: The south edge of the elongated classroom volume provides the directional facade anchor.

negative.statement: Correcting the ground level to negate the slope contradicts the constructive simplicity by requiring substantial foundations.

position.rationale: Ground-level placement is anchored to the lower sampled envelope and site-facing footprint.
